title: Statement on the Hepatotoxicity of Green Tea Catechins - Key studies described by EFSA in their Opinion | Committee on Toxicity
abstract: In a 14-week toxicity study (n=10/sex/group) in which rats were administered a GTE (ethanol:water extraction of green tea leaves, resulting in an EGCG content of 48.4%) by oral gavage, 5 days/week, the NOAEL for liver toxicity was 500 mg GTE/kg bw per day – equivalent to 242 mg EGCG/kg bw per day (Chan et al., 2010). In a 13-week study in dogs, an EGCG preparation (80% EGCG) was administered by capsule at doses of 0, 50, 150 and 500 mg/kg bw per day (corresponding to 0, 40, 120 or 400 mg EGCG/kg bw per day) to groups of fasted male and female animals (Isbrucker et al., 2006). In a second, 13-week study reported in the same paper (Isbrucker et al., 2006), groups of fed male and female dogs received capsules containing re-crystallized EGCG (91.8% purity) at doses of 0, 50, 300, or 500 mg/kg bw per day.
